title: Natural single-source internal Hom chain comparison
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. The cochain-complex functor $K\mapsto\mathcal Hom^\bullet(M[0],K)$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is naturally isomorphic to termwise application of $\mathcal Hom(M,-)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] to cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. The postcomposition functor is additive as in [lem-sc-hom-complex-single]. No boundedness or exactness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section 0A8X, section-hom-complexes: product, differential and map formulas; parent comparison proof step 2

proof.text: For the single complex M[0], define the degree-n map to Hom(M,K^n) by the degree-zero source projection of homComplex_exists. All other source factors are zero. The product universal property supplies the inverse by inserting the inverse identification at source degree zero and zero elsewhere. This is the construction in lem-sc-hom-complex-single, not an arbitrary choice of its objectwise isomorphisms.

The Hom-complex differential formula shows that these projections commute with differentials: the source differential is zero, leaving exactly postcomposition with the target differential. The Hom-complex map formula, applied to the identity of M[0] and an arbitrary chain map f:K→K′, identifies map(f) followed by the degree-zero projection with the projection followed by postcomposition with f. Therefore the chain isomorphisms form a natural isomorphism. The argument works degree by degree, including zero M, zero target, an empty scheme, and arbitrary unbounded targets.

proof_origin.place: Section 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, map formula specialized to the identity of the degree-zero source

theorem homComplex_single_natural_iso
    (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (P : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) :
    Nonempty ((homComplexFunctor (R := Y.sheaf)).obj
        (op ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj P)) ≅
      ((SheafOfModules.homFunctor Y.sheaf).obj (op P)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))
